marks.note: States that dai /dai/ 'has an extra /i/ glide'. Against di /di/, the sound dai adds is the vowel /a/ (d-a-i); the /i/ is in both words. Should read: 'dai has an extra /a/ before the /i/'. The listening item still works.

'In questa città è un museo molto famoso.' Bare essere meaning 'there is' is literary but it is still current in written descriptive and guidebook prose ('Nella cappella è un affresco di Giotto'), so an educated reader may accept the sentence; in speech it is c'è. Replace it with a clear misuse, for example 'Sono freddo, chiudi la finestra' (avere freddo).

qualche: 'Ho perso qualche treno delle otto e sono arrivato tardi' can be read as grammatical and meaningful (on a few days I missed the 8 o'clock train and was late). The passato prossimo does not force a single event, so a native may accept a second option. Replace it with a distractor that the meaning clearly excludes, or add 'stamattina' to the frame.
troppo: 'troppo capo' (troppo with a singular count noun) is ruled out by grammar alone. The profile's level_3 rule says the wrong options must fail on meaning only.
quanto: 'Quando arriva quanto capo' is ungrammatical, so it fails on grammar, not meaning (profile level_3 rule). The explanation's reasoning about a question 'about quantity' is strained.

nessun: a postverbal nessun without non is ungrammatical, which is grammar, not meaning (the explanation itself calls it valency). For a determiner every real meaning distractor (un, quel, questo) also fits, so level_3 on il cannot satisfy the profile rule. Consider declining level_3 for articles.
alcun: it is excluded only because the sentence is affirmative, so it fails on grammar, not meaning (profile level_3 rule).

'Ho solo cinque euro, quindi non posso comprare il libro.' This is a perfectly correct, natural sentence. Solo is the adverb 'only', a different word, and it is not misused. Every native accepts it, so the item has two correct sentences. Replace it with a sentence that a native rejects and in which the adjective solo is misused for meaning.

'Oggi c'è il sole, quindi andiamo al mare.' It is correct Italian and does not contain the target word at all: sole here is the noun 'sun'. It cannot be a misuse of solo, and a learner who picks it is right.

'Ho visto quel film una sola volta, ma lo ricordo bene.' This is correct and natural: una sola volta = only once is a standard use of the adjective solo. The explanation even says so ('a different sense'). It is not wrong, so the item has two correct answers.
It says 'per volta means each time'. That is false: per volta means 'at a time' (uno per volta, due alla volta). 'Each time' is ogni volta. The option itself is correctly wrong.

patterns: level_6 'wrong' sentences that are correct Italian: the word in another sense or another part of speech (solo 'only', una sola volta) or a homograph that is not the target at all (sole 'sun'). This makes the semantic-discrimination item have several right answers. It is the most serious class, and it accounts for 3 of the 4 wrong units in solo.

level_3 cloze distractors for function words (il) that are ruled out by grammar alone (troppo, quanto, nessun, alcun), against the profile rule. Where a distractor was meant to fail on meaning it may in fact fit (qualche treno delle otto). For articles every meaning-level alternative (un, quel, questo) is grammatical, so level_3 for determiners is structurally weak and should probably be declined.
English explanations with a false linguistic claim while the option itself is right: di 'dai has an extra /i/ glide' (it is /a/), solo 'per volta means each time' (it means at a time).

level_6 wrong sentences that are only literary or marked rather than wrong (bare existential essere 'In questa città è un museo'). Also, for cosa, sound-alike malapropisms (casa, a causa di, costa) are used in place of real sense misuses. They are clearly wrong and so acceptable, but they test form recognition more than meaning.

level_1 explanations saying 'the rest is the same' ignore the open/closed vowel (polo, molo, sodo /ɔ/ against solo /o/; coda /o/ against cosa /ɔ/) and s/z voicing (rosa, posa). This follows the profile's policy of not drilling these contrasts, so it is not marked, but strictly speaking the statements are approximate.

Grammar drill: level labels that are too high (lvl 3 items with one clause of A2 words: 009, 050). Several items reuse the same frame as another item in the batch (017/032 fireworks, 028/033 post offices, 013/048 and 023/048 Lei + sicuro, 012/049 pronte/pronta per la visita, 007/040 il problema serio, 018/050 uova fresche, 019/045 blu). The sentences are not identical, but the batch rule asks for no shared sentences and the near-duplicates reduce variety. These were not marked individually.
